newsitem.title: USA: Ferrofluidics says SEC to punish ex-holders.
newsitem.headline: Ferrofluidics says SEC to punish ex-holders.

text.p: Ferrofluidics Corp said Wednesday the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has inititated administrative and cease-and-desist proceedings against three former holders in a 1992 private placement.
The company said the proceedings involve Paul Okuda, Stephen Thorpe and David Chester.

The SEC alleges the three participated in a scheme with the company's former chief executive and chief financial officers, Ronald Moskowitz and Jan Kirk, to create the false appearance that Ferrofluidics has sold 620,000 shares in the private placement, the company said in a press release.

The company said the SEC's allegations arise from an investigation begun in 1993. The SEC ordered the company to undertake a private investigation, which Ferrofluidics appointed a special committee to handle, it said.

As a result of the investigation, Moskowitz and Kirk left the company in 1993 and the company restated its financial statements for fiscal years 1991, 1992 and 1993, it said. The investigations also prompted class action lawsuits by shareholders, which the company said it settled in 1994.
